venue_from_text: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, Boston, MA

stops.title: The Rape of Europa
stops.story_quote: In 1917, the sculptor Paul Manship sent Gardner a bronze relief inspired by The Rape of Europa
specifics_traced: Titian, oil on canvas, signature TITIANVS.P. (documented)
Manship 1917 bronze relief gift (confirmed true, Gardner Museum blog/collection page)
Jupiter as a white bull abducting Europa (documented myth/painting subject)

stops.title: Chez Tortoni
stops.story_quote: Louis Kronberg purchased Chez Tortoni at auction in Paris in 1922...his acquisition brought this work into the collection
specifics_traced: Kronberg purchased it at the Kélékian auction, 1922, through American artist Louis Kronberg (confirmed, Gardner Museum)

fabrications.claim: Kronberg purchased Chez Tortoni 'at auction in Paris in 1922'
fabrications.why: Gardner Museum provenance: bought at the American Art Association (Kélékian sale), New York, Jan 1922, through Louis Kronberg — not Paris

stops.title: The Story of Lucretia
stops.story_quote: a moment that traditionally symbolizes the end of tyranny and the birth of the Roman Republic
specifics_traced: Botticelli, tempera and oil on panel, c.1500 (documented)
Lucretia legend tied to founding of the Roman Republic (documented)

stops.title: A Lady and Gentleman in Black
stops.story_quote: On March 18, 1990, an unknown thief entered...and cut A Lady and Gentleman in Black from its stretcher
specifics_traced: Bernard Berenson acquired it for Gardner (documented)

stops.title: The Concert
stops.story_quote: The void recalls the absence of other masterpieces taken during the same heist, such as...The Storm on the Sea of Galilee
specifics_traced: Vermeer, c.1664, one of 34 known works (documented)
Storm on the Sea of Galilee also stolen in 1990 (documented)

stops.title: Landscape with Obelisk
stops.story_quote: This painting was once attributed to Rembrandt, reflecting the close stylistic ties and shared workshop
specifics_traced: Govert Flinck, 1638, oil on panel 54.5x71cm (confirmed, Wikipedia/FBI art file)
long attributed to Rembrandt, later reattributed (confirmed)

defects: Wrong auction city (Paris vs New York) at stop 2
one_line_verdict: Clean, well-sourced, all real works at this venue; one wrong city in a provenance line; strong story content.
